text: 無駄のない計画だろ? / 俺に踏んだよ。
translation: A flawless plan, right? / You stepped on me.

vocabulary.meaning: right?, isn't it? (casual form of だろう, seeking agreement)
to step on, to tread on

grammar: 無駄のない is a noun-modifying phrase: 無駄 (waste) + の + ない (not existing) → 'having no waste.' だろ is a casual contraction of だろう used to seek confirmation. 俺に踏んだよ: に marks the target/point of contact, よ adds mild assertion.

text: すごい稚園の召喚師様らしいな
translation: Apparently she's some incredible young summoner.

vocabulary.meaning: honorific suffix (respectful, often for high-status persons)
apparently, it seems that (inferential, based on hearsay or evidence)
sentence-final particle expressing light reflection or mild emphasis

grammar: らしい expresses inference or hearsay — the speaker is reporting what they've heard, not something directly witnessed. 様 here is an honorific title attached to 召喚士, showing deep respect. Note: 稚園 in the text appears to be a mishear/transcription error; context suggests 若い (young) or similar was intended.

text: おう、あのブラスカ様のご息女だ / すげえ
translation: Yeah, she's the daughter of that great Lord Braska. / Whoa.

vocabulary.meaning: that (well-known), the famous (used to refer to someone widely known)
incredible, amazing (very casual/rough form of すごい)

grammar: あの before a name implies the person is so famous the listener surely knows them — 'that renowned Lord Braska.' ご息女 uses the honorific prefix ご + 息女 (daughter), a very formal/respectful term. すげえ is a colloquial phonetic shift from すごい, common in casual male speech.

text: ブラスカ様の娘?
translation: Lord Braska's daughter?
grammar: A short exclamatory question with rising intonation — the question mark alone carries the interrogative meaning. No verb is needed; the noun phrase itself functions as a surprised question.

text: ユーナの親って有名人なのか?
translation: Is Yuna's parent a famous person?

vocabulary.meaning: topic marker (casual form of は/と言う); 'as for,' 'speaking of'
is it that…? (interrogative with explanatory の)

grammar: って is a casual topic-marking particle, equivalent to は in formal speech. なのか is an interrogative with の (explanatory/softening) + か (question marker), giving a tone of genuine curiosity or slight surprise.

text: 大召喚師ブラスカ様の娘だ / 神にご生存あった
translation: She's the daughter of Great Summoner Lord Braska. / He was blessed by the gods.

vocabulary.meaning: life, living (highly honorific form of 生存)

grammar: 大 as a prefix intensifies the title — 大召喚士 means 'Great Summoner,' the highest rank. ご生存 uses honorific prefix ご with 生存 (existence/life). Note: this second line appears to be a somewhat garbled or archaic-sounding phrase expressing that Braska was divinely favored.

text: 10年前にシンを倒した大召喚士 ブラスカ様
translation: Great Summoner Lord Braska, who defeated Sin ten years ago.

vocabulary.meaning: to defeat, to bring down, to topple
Great Summoner (highest honorific title for a summoner)

grammar: The sentence is a noun phrase, not a full sentence — ブラスカ様 is the head noun, modified by the relative clause 10年前にシンを倒した. This structure (relative clause + noun) is standard Japanese: the modifying clause precedes the noun it describes.

text: ユーナは召喚士として最高の血を受け継いでるのさ
translation: As a summoner, Yuna has inherited the finest bloodline.

vocabulary.meaning: to inherit, to succeed to, to carry on
explanatory sentence-final particle (の + さ, adds a knowing or explanatory tone)

grammar: として marks role or capacity — 召喚士として = 'in her role as a summoner.' 受け継いでる is a contracted form of 受け継いでいる (te-form + いる = ongoing state). のさ adds an explanatory, slightly authoritative tone — the speaker is explaining something they know well.

text: かわいそうだよな 親が有名だと
translation: It must be tough when your parents are famous, huh.

vocabulary.meaning: right?, huh (よ + な, expressing shared feeling or seeking agreement)
when/if ~ is the case (conditional; sets up the preceding main clause)

grammar: The sentence order is reversed for emphasis: かわいそうだよな (main sentiment) comes first, then 親が有名だと (the conditional/reason) follows. This is common in colloquial Japanese — the emotional reaction precedes the cause. だと is a conditional ('when/if it is the case that...').

text: この人にそういう想像力を期待しても 無駄ね
translation: It's pointless expecting that kind of empathy from this person.

vocabulary.meaning: that kind of, such (referring to something just mentioned)
to expect, to hope for, to anticipate
even if (one) does ~; concessive te-form + も
sentence-final particle expressing shared observation or mild emphasis

grammar: 〜しても is a concessive construction: 'even if you do X, (it's still the case that)...' Here: 'even if you expect it from this person, it's pointless.' This is Lulu's sharp, dismissive remark about Wakka. ね at the end softens the bluntness slightly, or invites the listener to agree.

text: 覚えとくよ ルル
translation: I'll keep that in mind, Lulu.

vocabulary.meaning: to remember, to memorize, to keep in mind
to do something in advance / to keep something done (preparatory nuance)

grammar: 覚えとく is a contraction of 覚えておく (te-form + おく). おく here implies intentionally keeping something stored away — 'I'll file that away.' よ asserts mild resolution. Wakka is responding to Lulu's criticism with a touch of wounded dignity.

text: 火星、気持ちいいね
translation: The breeze feels great, doesn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: right?, doesn't it (seeking agreement or sharing a feeling)

grammar: 気持ちいい is a contracted form of 気持ちがいい. Note: 火星 normally means 'Mars (planet)'; here it is likely a transcription error for 潮風 (しおかぜ, sea breeze) or 海風 (かいふう), which fits the on-ship context. ね invites the listener to share the pleasant feeling.

text: ブリッツの選手なんでしょ?ザナルカンドの / それ、ワッカから聞いた?
translation: You're a blitzball player, aren't you? From Zanarkand. / Did you hear that from Wakka?

vocabulary.meaning: aren't you?, right? (casual confirmation-seeking, softened by でしょ)
to hear, to listen, to ask

grammar: なんでしょ is a softened confirmation question: なん (=な explanatory) + でしょ (casual でしょう). It assumes the answer is yes but gently checks. ザナルカンドの at the end is a trailing noun phrase — the の implies 'from Zanarkand,' left hanging for natural effect. 〜から聞いた = 'heard from ~.'

text: あいつ、絶対信じてないくせに
translation: He totally doesn't believe it, yet he goes around saying that.

vocabulary.meaning: that guy, he/she (casual, slightly rough third-person pronoun)
even though, despite the fact that (implies criticism or contradiction)

grammar: くせに attaches to a verb/adjective/noun and expresses indignant contradiction — 'even though he [does/is X], he [does Y].' It carries a resentful or accusatory nuance, stronger than のに. Here Tidus is annoyed that Wakka told Yuna about Zanarkand while clearly not believing it himself.

text: 私は信じるよ
translation: I believe you.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle asserting or affirming (adds warmth or conviction here)

grammar: 私は provides explicit contrast with the previous statement about Wakka — 'I (for my part) believe you.' は here is contrastive. よ adds gentle conviction. A short, sincere line from Yuna.

text: ザナルカンドでは / 夜でも光があふれていて / 大きなスタジアムがあって
translation: In Zanarkand, / even at night the lights overflow, / and there's a huge stadium,

vocabulary.meaning: in ~, at ~ (topic/location marker with contrastive nuance)
even ~, even in the case of ~
to overflow, to be full to bursting, to be abundant
te-form of ている; continuing/connecting to next clause
big, large (prenominal form of 大きい)

grammar: This is a series of て-form connected clauses building a vivid picture. あふれていて is ている (ongoing state) in te-form, linking to the next clause. 夜でも uses でも for 'even' — 'even at night.' The sentence is left open, continuing into the next clip.

text: スタジアムではブリッツボールの試合が開かれて
translation: blitzball matches are held in the stadium,

vocabulary.meaning: to be held, to be opened (passive of 開く)

grammar: 開かれる is the passive form of 開く (to open/hold). In Japanese, events being 'held' often use the passive: 試合が開かれる = 'matches are held.' The て at the end continues the chain of clauses from the previous segment.

text: いつも超満員 / なんで知ってんのさ / ジェクトという人から聞いたの
translation: always packed to capacity. / How do you know that? / I heard it from someone named Jecht.

vocabulary.meaning: casual contraction of 〜ているの; interrogative explanatory ending
sentence-final particle (casual; slightly insistent or curious)

grammar: 超満員 uses 超 as a colloquial intensifier (common in younger/casual speech). 知ってんの is a contraction of 知っているの — the ているの becomes てんの in fast speech. のさ at the end of なんで知ってんのさ adds a slightly probing, curious tone. ジェクトという人 = 'a person called Jecht' — という is used to name or identify.

text: 父さんが旅を守ってくれた人
translation: The person who protected my father on his journey.

vocabulary.meaning: to protect, to guard, to defend
to do (something) for me/us (benefactive; expresses gratitude for an action)

grammar: 〜てくれた expresses that someone did something for the speaker's benefit (or the benefit of someone close to the speaker). 守ってくれた人 = 'the person who protected [him] for us.' The whole phrase is a noun phrase — no main predicate verb — completing Yuna's explanation of who Jecht was to her.

text: 俺の親父もジェクトって言うんだ
translation: My old man is also called Jecht.

vocabulary.meaning: is called ~, goes by the name of ~
explanatory sentence ending (adds revelation or personal context)

grammar: 〜って言う (ともいう) is a colloquial way to say 'is called' or 'goes by the name of.' も is used for 'also' — Tidus is noting the shared name. んだ marks this as a personal revelation or explanation, giving it a 'you see...' nuance.

text: すごい
translation: Wow.

text: 私たちが出会えたのはきっとエヴォンの賜物だね
translation: Our meeting was surely a gift from Yevon.

vocabulary.meaning: to meet, to encounter, to come across
to be able to meet (potential form of 出会う)
isn't it, right (casual affirmation seeking light agreement)

grammar: 出会えたのは nominalized with の: 'the fact that we were able to meet.' This nominalizer の turns the verb phrase into the subject. きっと strengthens certainty. 賜物 is a formal/literary word, fitting for a religious context — Yuna is framing their encounter in terms of Yevon's blessing.

text: 似てるけど別人だよ
translation: They're similar, but different people.

vocabulary.meaning: a different person, someone else entirely

grammar: 似てる is a contraction of 似ている. けど here is a mild concessive conjunction: 'similar, but...' The brevity of the line gives it a firm, almost resigned tone — Tidus is shutting down the idea that his father and Yuna's Jecht are the same person.

text: どうして?
translation: Why?

text: 親父、死んだんだ
translation: My old man is dead.

vocabulary.meaning: explanatory/emphatic ending (adds emotional weight or personal explanation)

grammar: んだ at the end of a completed action (死んだ) adds an explanatory or emotionally laden nuance — it's not a neutral statement of fact but a personal revelation with feeling behind it. Tidus is explaining why they can't be the same person.

text: 10年前、ザナルカンドの海でな
translation: Ten years ago, in the sea off Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle (masculine, reflective; softens or adds wistfulness)

grammar: The sentence is a fragment — no verb — continuing from the previous line (親父、死んだんだ). な at the end gives it a quiet, reflective tone, often associated with male speech. The whole line functions as a trailing elaboration: 'ten years ago, in the sea off Zanarkand [he died]...'

text: そっか…
translation: I see…

vocabulary.meaning: I see, oh (casual contraction of そうか; expresses quiet understanding)

grammar: そっか is a contraction of そうか (literally 'is that so'). The trailing ellipsis marks a pause — Yuna absorbing the weight of what Tidus just said. A simple but emotionally resonant line.

text: ある日、海へトレーニングに行ったまま、帰ってこなかった
translation: One day he went to the sea to train and never came back.

vocabulary.meaning: to go to do ~ (purpose of going)
having done ~ and staying in that state; left as is after doing ~

grammar: 〜たまま is a key grammar point: verb in た-form + まま = 'remaining in the state of having done X.' Here: 行ったまま = 'having gone and staying gone.' 帰ってこなかった = 'did not come back' (帰る + てくる negative past, emphasizing movement back toward the speaker's reference point).

text: それっきり行方不明さ
translation: After that, he was never heard from again.

vocabulary.meaning: after that, since then and no more; that was the last of it
sentence-final particle (casual, slightly resigned or matter-of-fact)

grammar: それっきり combines それ (that) + きり (only, just, since then) — a set expression meaning 'after that point, nothing more.' 行方不明 is a four-character compound: 行方 (whereabouts) + 不明 (unknown). さ at the end gives a resigned, 'that's just how it is' tone.

text: ジェクトさんは、その日にスピラに来たんだよ / まさか… / だって、私がJactさんに会ったのは10年と95日前。
translation: Jecht came to Spira on that very day. / No way… / Because, the day I met Jecht was 10 years and 95 days ago.

vocabulary.meaning: explanatory emphatic (の + だ + よ, adding conviction to an explanation)
no way, surely not, that can't be (expressing disbelief)
because, but (casual; introduces a reason or objection)

grammar: んだよ combines the explanatory の + だ + よ for strong explanatory assertion — Yuna is making a significant claim. まさか expresses stunned disbelief. 私がJectさんに会ったのは nominalized: 'the time I met Jecht' — の turns the clause into a noun, then は marks it as the topic. だって introduces Yuna's reasoning in a casual, slightly earnest way.

text: 父さんが旅立った日だから、よく覚えてる。
translation: I remember it well because it's the day my father set off on his journey.

vocabulary.meaning: to set out on a journey, to depart
because ~ is the case; therefore (causal conjunction)

grammar: 旅立った is the past tense of 旅立つ, modifying 日 (day): 'the day [father] departed.' だから here is causal — 'because it was [that] day, I remember it well.' The short sentence is natural and emotionally grounded — Yuna explaining why the date is etched in her memory.

text: 時期はぴったりでしょ?
translation: The timing matches perfectly, doesn't it?

vocabulary.meaning: right?, isn't it? (casual form of でしょう, seeking confirmation)

grammar: ぴったり is an onomatopoeic/mimetic adverb meaning 'exactly matching, snugly fitting.' It functions here as a predicate complement. でしょ (casual でしょう) seeks the listener's agreement.

text: でも、どうやって来たってんだよ。
translation: But, how the heck did he get here?

vocabulary.meaning: how, by what means, in what way
colloquial contraction of 〜というんだよ; emphatic/frustrated rhetorical question

grammar: どうやって is a set interrogative phrase: どう (how) + やって (te-form of やる, 'to do') = 'by doing how.' 〜ってんだ is a contraction of 〜と言うんだ, used in frustrated or emphatic rhetorical questions — 'how on earth is he supposed to have come here?' よ adds exasperation.

text: 君は、ここにいるよ。
translation: But you're here, aren't you.

vocabulary.meaning: you (informal, used to address someone you're familiar with)
to be, to exist (for animate beings)
sentence-final particle (mild assertion, pointing something out)

grammar: A quietly devastating counterpoint — Yuna's logic: if Tidus can be here without an obvious explanation, so could Jecht. よ gently points this out rather than pressing the argument aggressively. いる is used for animate beings, contrasting with ある for inanimate objects.

text: シーン!
translation: Sin!

vocabulary.meaning: Sin (the monstrous entity that periodically destroys civilization in Spira)

text: そりゃワイヤーフックだろうが! / そんなもん打ち込んでどうするよ!
translation: That's a wire hook! / What are you going to do sticking that thing in?!

vocabulary.meaning: that is (casual contraction of それは)
obviously it's ~!, it's clearly ~ (emphatic, indignant assertion)
such a thing, something like that (casual; often dismissive)
to drive into, to strike into, to embed
what will (you) do?, what's the point of (doing)?

grammar: だろうが is an emphatic variant of だろう, expressing indignant obviousness: 'It's obviously a wire hook!' そんなもん is a casual form of そんなもの. 打ち込んでどうする combines the te-form (indicating the action) + どうする (a rhetorical 'what's the point?') — 'by driving that in, what do you intend to do?'

text: 船ごと海に引きずり込まれるぞ! / シーンはキーリカに向かっている! / あいつの注意を引きつけたい!
translation: We'll get dragged into the sea along with the ship! / Sin is heading toward Kilika! / I want to draw its attention!

vocabulary.meaning: to drag into, to pull down into
sentence-final particle (strong assertion, warning, or excitement; masculine)
to head toward, to proceed in the direction of
to attract, to draw in, to captivate

grammar: 引きずり込まれる is a passive form of the compound verb 引きずり込む — 'to be dragged into.' ごと after a noun means 'together with, including the entirety of' — 船ごと = 'the ship and everything on it.' ぞ is a strong masculine assertion particle, here conveying urgency/warning. 注意を引きつけたい: 注意を引きつける = 'to attract attention'; たい marks the speaker's desire.

text: キリカには俺たちの家族が! / 将会様お命を!
translation: Our families are in Kilika! / Lord Commander, your orders!

vocabulary.meaning: honorific for 'life' or 'orders/command' (here: a call for the commander's order)

grammar: キリカには uses には for emphatic location + topic: 'in Kilika there are...' The sentence trails off (no verb) — the urgency makes the full statement unnecessary. 将会様お命を is an archaic/formal phrasing — 将 (commander) + 会様 (honorific) + お命を (imploring for command/orders). The whole phrase reads as a desperate plea: 'My lord, give the order!'
